title: The two-minute start
description: When a task feels too big to face, promise yourself only two minutes. Starting is the hard part; two minutes is a door, not a demand.

body.heading: Why two minutes works
paragraphs: Big tasks trigger big resistance. Two minutes is too small to argue with, so the argument never starts. You are not committing to the whole job, just to opening it.
Once you are inside the task, the picture changes. The dreaded thing usually turns out to be a series of ordinary steps, and continuing for a while longer feels natural rather than forced.

body.heading: Keep the promise honest
paragraphs: The deal must be real: after two minutes you are genuinely allowed to stop. If the permission is fake, your brain will stop believing the offer and the trick stops working.
Some days you will stop at two minutes, and that is a success, not a loophole. You touched the task, kept the streak alive, and made tomorrow's start easier.

takeaway: Promise two honest minutes; most days, momentum does the rest.
